title: Git, dependencies and reproducible runs

objectives.text: Inspect working-tree changes and create an intentional source checkpoint without committing secrets.
Record and recreate a declared runtime/dependency setup while distinguishing isolation from reproducibility.

blocks.markdown: A useful result names the code and environment that produced it. Git records source snapshots; it does not automatically capture your Python runtime, database, untracked data or shell state. Before committing, inspect git status and git diff. Add intended files explicitly, then inspect the staged diff with git diff --cached. Do not assume git add . is a safe default in a folder containing credentials or large generated data.

blocks.source:
git status --short
git diff
git add fee.py test_fee.py
git diff --cached
git commit -m "Test exact-cent fee contract"
blocks.caption: Illustrative commands for your own exercise repository after those files exist. Commit only intended files. Output depends on repository state; no fixed success output is claimed.

blocks.markdown: Keep tokens, passwords and private data out of source control. A .gitignore rule helps prevent accidental addition of currently untracked files; it does not remove a secret already tracked or erase it from history. If a credential was exposed, removing the file in a later commit is not enough: revoke/rotate the credential and follow the applicable incident procedure. No learner task here asks you to paste a secret.

A virtual environment isolates installed Python packages for a project. It is not a container or a complete machine snapshot. The same source may still behave differently across Python/library versions, OS/native libraries or external services. Record the versions actually tested and use a dependency manifest with appropriate version constraints or a lock process for the chosen tool.

blocks.source:
python3 -m venv .venv
# POSIX shell activation:
. .venv/bin/activate
python --version
python -m pip --version
# Use the project's reviewed dependency file if one is provided:
# python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
blocks.caption: Optional local setup. Windows activation differs. This module uses only the standard library, so installing third-party packages is not needed to run its examples. Commands may require local permissions and are not browser actions.

blocks.source:
import platform
import sys
print(sys.implementation.name)
print(platform.python_version())
blocks.caption: Prints the implementation and runtime version actually in use. The exact version is environment-dependent; it must not be memorised as a universal output.

blocks.markdown: A reproducible handover includes the source revision, run command, tested runtime, dependency resolution, input data/hash where appropriate, seeds and expected results with tolerances. Pinning package versions alone may not freeze transitive dependencies, platform wheels or external data. A seed does not guarantee identical output across every library version or parallel implementation. State the conditions under which you checked reproduction.

Creating an environment does not install an uncached package while offline. These lessons remain readable offline; standard-library examples can be copied into a compatible local runtime. A browser code runner must explicitly report its capability and runtime availability rather than pretending a failed install is the learner's wrong answer.

Independent transfer: create a local exercise folder if you have Git/Python installed, save fee.py and its tests, inspect changes, run the tests and write a short RUN.md naming the command/runtime and synthetic input. If local tools are unavailable, inspect the supplied commands and identify which files/state a Git commit does and does not capture. The local-tool task is not a gate on reading the next lesson.

Technical references: [Git status](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-status) for status; [Git diff](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff) for working-tree and staged comparisons; [gitignore](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitignore) for the untracked-file scope and tracked-file limitation; [Python venv](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/venv.html) for environment isolation. Reproduction and incident-handling tasks are declared engineering guidance, not claims that Git or venv captures a complete machine or handles exposed credentials automatically.

summary: Record source and environment separately. Inspect staged changes, never commit secrets, and do not equate a virtual environment or one seed with complete reproducibility.
